newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels in huge attack against troops.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels in huge attack against troops.

text.p: Separatist Tamil rebels launched a pre-dawn assault on the military's defences near the northern town of Vavuniya on Tuesday in a bid to cut off supplies to troops fighting further north, the Defence Ministry said.
It said more than 500 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels attacked the military's forward defence line at Thandikulam just north of the government-controlled frontline town of Vavuniya.
Vavuniya is 220 km (135 miles) north of Colombo.

A Defence Ministry statement said it was evident the LTTE were trying to dislodge the military's field headquarters and artillery positions at Thandikulam to disrupt an ongoing offensive against the rebels.
"But troops fought back valiantly to repulse the attack, causing very heavy casualties among the terrorists," it said.

Military officials said the rebels blew up a key bridge at Nochchomoddai, just north of Thandikulam, from where security forces had launched Operation "Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", on the rebels' northern Wanni stronghold nearly one month ago.
An ammunition dump was destroyed when a rebel mortar round hit it, the ministry statement said.
Officials said at least four soldiers were killed and more than 20 were wounded in the attack. They were not sure how many rebels had been killed, but said they expected LTTE casualties to be heavy.

An aid worker in Vavuniya told Reuters that three civilians, including a seven-year-old girl, had been killed in the fighting. Some 28 people were wounded and admitted to the Vavuniya hospital, he said.
The Defence Ministry said detalis of casualties would be known only after clearing operations were completed.
Mi-24 helicopter gunships and Pucara ground attack craft had fired at the rebels from the air, causing them to flee into nearby jungles, the officials said.
The rebels had fired about 25 artillery rounds, some of which exploded near the Vavuniya air force base but caused little damage, they added.
A Defence Ministry spokesman said the attack would not be a setback to troops who had already captured several rebel-held towns in the shrub-covered Wanni, driving the LTTE further north.

"By this evening, we will take full control of the situation (at Nochchimoddai), allowing troops to carry on with the offensive," he said. "We have enough troops to guard the rear and advance at the same time."
Independent confirmation of the events was not possible as the media have not been allowed into the war zone.
The LTTE's spokesmen in London were not immediately available for comment.

A separate Defence Ministry statement said troops that had advanced about 20 km (12.5 miles) north from Nochchimoddai into the rebel heartland on Tuesday were consolidating positions in newly captured areas.
Some 20,000 government troops are advancing on two flanks into the rebel stronghold in an offensive launched on May 13.
Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte said last week that the offensive's aim was to open a land supply route to Jaffna, 100 km (60 miles) further north of Vavuniya.
Troops captured the LTTE's former stronghold of Jaffna last year in a major offensive, driving the rebels into the Wanni.
The LTTE are fighting for a homeland for minority Tamils in mostly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the etnic war, now in its 14th year. The rebels say the toll is higher.
